sources.observed: Existing Sea Bright USGS 01407600 hourly-max archive
sources.seaLevelScenarios: NOAA CO-OPS 2022 Interagency Sea Level Report station projections
sources.localObservedTrend: Equal-weight monthly means of the existing hourly-max archive; hourly maxima may bias the mean.

method.historic: Local maxima in contiguous hourly-max records, separated by at least six hours with 0.2 ft prominence; gauge exceedances, not documented property flood events.
method.baselineRebase: each observed local-gauge peak adjusted to 1 January 2026 using the fitted local observed trend
method.seaLevelCurves: quadratic least-squares fits to each NOAA 2022 median scenario, evaluated annually and rebased to zero in 2026; the observed local trend remains linear
method.cdf: continuous Gaussian-kernel CDF fitted to present-year-rebased independent high-tide peaks
method.uncertainty: two-sided 95 percent calendar-year block-bootstrap percentile interval for the fitted exceedance probability at every elevation, year, and curve
method.future: continuous fitted CDF probability of water level being strictly greater than screening elevation plus 0.1 foot, with its 95 percent bounds multiplied by 705 expected astronomical high tides per year

floodDefinition.elevationRule: Local five-foot terrain at NSI structure point plus USACE modeled foundation height; parcel representative point if no structure is matched.

observedTrendFit.method: ordinary least squares on equal-weight monthly means of the existing Sea Bright hourly-max archive

limitations: Screening estimate, not surveyed first-floor elevation or validated property flood history.
Projected counts assume a stationary tide distribution shifted by relative sea-level change; do not include changing storm climatology, waves, or future defenses.
Bootstrap range describes sample variation only; excludes floor, terrain, sea-level-scenario and hydraulic-model uncertainty.
No inference that a parcel is hydrologically connected solely because a gauge exceeds its floor.
